```{r}
# Install packages if necessary
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "broom", "ggplot2", "car", "interactions", "psych", "lmtest"))

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)
library(interactions)
library(psych)
library(lmtest)
```

```{r}
# Import the dataset
# put ur dataset in the same folder as the rmd file
data <- read.csv("data.csv")
```

## Part A: Single Pathway Analysis
### 1. Inspect the dataset
```{r}
head(data)
str(data)
dim(data)
names(data)
summary(data)

# Check missing values for each variable
colSums(is.na(data))

# Check duplicate participant IDs
sum(duplicated(data$ID))
```

```{r}
# Check whether values fall within the ranges
# specified in the assignment
summary(data$StatsCourses)
summary(data$GradeStats)
summary(data$Judgment)
summary(data$Comprehension)

# Check categorical variables
table(data$Sexe, useNA = "ifany")
table(data$GoalStudy, useNA = "ifany")
```

### 2. Descriptive Statistics
```{r}
data %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_stats_courses = mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_stats_courses = sd(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_judgment = mean(Judgment, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_judgment = sd(Judgment, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_comprehension = mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_comprehension = sd(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Distribution of the outcome variable
ggplot(data, aes(x = Judgment)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Judgement Scores",
    x = "Number of correct judgements",
    y = "Number of participants"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Association between statistics credits and judgement
ggplot(data, aes(x = StatsCourses, y = Judgment)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Statistics Credits and Fake-News Detection",
    x = "Statistics course credits (ECs)",
    y = "Correct judgements"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 3. Prepare the analysis dataset
```{r}
# do not automatically remove participants based on
# comprehension or guessed study purpose
# First inspect missingness and justify any exclusions.

analysis_data <- data %>%
  select(ID, StatsCourses, Judgment, Comprehension) %>%
  drop_na()

nrow(analysis_data)
```

### 4. RQ1
```{r}
# Association between statistics credits
# and the number of correct judgements

model_rq1 <- lm(
  Judgment ~ StatsCourses,
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(model_rq1)
confint(model_rq1)

# Check basic linear-model diagnostics
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_rq1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### 5. RQ2
```{r}
# Does comprehension moderate the association?
# Center the continuous predictors to aid interpretation

analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension)
  )

model_rq2 <- lm(
  Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c,
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(model_rq2)
confint(model_rq2)

# Inspect the interaction visually
ggplot(
  analysis_data,
  aes(
    x = StatsCourses,
    y = Judgment,
    color = factor(
      if_else(Comprehension >= median(Comprehension),
              "Higher comprehension", "Lower comprehension")
    )
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Statistics course credits (ECs)",
    y = "Correct judgements",
    color = "Comprehension group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# 8. Extract model estimates for reporting

tidy(model_rq1, conf.int = TRUE)
tidy(model_rq2, conf.int = TRUE)

glance(model_rq1)
glance(model_rq2)
```

## Part 2: Check Computational Reproducitibility
### 1. Inspect the dataset
```{r}
# Check how many participants are in each category
table(data$GoalStudy)

# Check statistics grades
summary(data$GradeStats)
```

### 2. Prepare the dataset, one with 5.5 as the passing-grade threshold,
### another one with 6.0
```{r}
# Remove participants who guessed the study goal
# and participants with a non-passing statistics grade

clean_data_1 <- data %>%
  filter(GoalStudy == 0,
         GradeStats >= 5.5)

# Check remaining sample size
nrow(clean_data_1)

# Check the cleaned dataset
summary(clean_data_1)
```

```{r}
# Try 6.0 as the passing grade
clean_data_2 <- data %>%
  filter(GoalStudy == 0,
         GradeStats >= 6.0)

# Check remaining sample size
nrow(clean_data_2)

# Check the cleaned dataset
summary(clean_data_2)
```

```{r}
# Check how many people is removed
nrow(data) - nrow(clean_data_1)
nrow(data) - nrow(clean_data_2)
```

### 3. Descriptive Statistics
```{r}
# Descriptive statistics
describe(clean_data_1[, c("StatsCourses",
                        "GradeStats",
                        "ReadNews",
                        "Judgment",
                        "Comprehension")])

# Correlation matrix
cor(clean_data_1[, c("StatsCourses",
                   "ReadNews",
                   "Judgment",
                   "Comprehension")],
    use = "complete.obs")
```

```{r}
# Descriptive statistics
describe(clean_data_2[, c("StatsCourses",
                        "GradeStats",
                        "ReadNews",
                        "Judgment",
                        "Comprehension")])

# Correlation matrix
cor(clean_data_2[, c("StatsCourses",
                   "ReadNews",
                   "Judgment",
                   "Comprehension")],
    use = "complete.obs")
```

### 4. rq1
```{r}
# Model 1.2: Linear regression with 5.5 as passing grade

model1_1 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses + ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_1)

# View results
summary(model1_1)
```

```{r}
# Model 1: Linear regression with 6.0 as passing grade

model1_2 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses + ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_2)

# View results
summary(model1_2)
```

## 5. rq2
```{r}
# Mean-centering
clean_data_1 <- clean_data_1 %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
clean_data_2 <- clean_data_2 %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
# Model 2.1: Moderation analysis with 5.5 as passing grade

model2_1 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c +
               ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_1)

# View results
summary(model2_1)
```

```{r}
# Model 2.2: Moderation analysis with 6.0 as passing grade

model2_2 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c +
               ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_2)

# View results
summary(model2_2)
```

```{r}
# Plot interaction

interact_plot(
  model2_1,
  pred = StatsCourses_c,
  modx = Comprehension_c,
  plot.points = TRUE,
  interval = TRUE,
  x.label = "Statistics course credits",
  y.label = "Fake news detection ability",
  modx.label = "Reading comprehension"
)

interact_plot(
  model2_2,
  pred = StatsCourses_c,
  modx = Comprehension_c,
  plot.points = TRUE,
  interval = TRUE,
  x.label = "Statistics course credits",
  y.label = "Fake news detection ability",
  modx.label = "Reading comprehension"
)
```

### 6. Regression assumptions check
```{r}
# Linearity
plot(model2_1, which=1)
plot(model2_2, which=1)
```

```{r}
# Normality of residuals
plot(model2_1, which=2)
plot(model2_1, which=2)
```

```{r}
# Homoscedasticity
bptest(model2_1)
bptest(model2_2)
```

```{r}
# Multicollinearity
vif(model2_1)
vif(model2_2)
```
